title: closeLoop
responsibility: Abandons a loop only when it still has pending steps, updates its closure timestamp and trace, and leaves step states unchanged.

inputs.name: closeLoopAbandoned.input
inputs.description: The input gives the loop to abandon as a lowercase kebab-case name (surrounding whitespace is trimmed) that selects specification/loops/<loop>/loop.json, and the abandon reason, which is trimmed, must not be empty, and is stored in closed.reason and the trace event. The optional root defaults to process.cwd(), the optional now defaults to new Date().toISOString() for closed.closedAt and updatedAt, and the loop must be open with at least one pending step.

examples.reason: Scope dropped after the planning review.

outputs.name: closeLoopAbandoned
outputs.description: Resolves to the closed loop state, with closed set to { status: 'abandoned', reason, closedAt } and updatedAt set to the same closedAt, plus tracePath, the trace file path relative to root. Steps, their statuses and their evidence come back unchanged, because only closed and updatedAt change.

errors.name: ExpectedCliError
errors.description: Thrown by fail() for expected problems, with a message meant for the user: an invalid loop name or empty abandon reason, a missing loop ('Loop does not exist.'), an invalid loop.json ('Invalid loop state: ...'), a state whose name differs from its directory, a loop that is already closed, or a loop with no pending steps.

errors.name: SyntaxError
errors.description: Thrown by JSON.parse when loop.json is not valid JSON; readLoop propagates it unchanged because only a missing file is converted to ExpectedCliError.

errors.name: ExpectedCliError
errors.description: Node.js file-system error from reading loop.json (other than ENOENT), writing loop.json or appending trace.ndjson; it is propagated unchanged and is not an ExpectedCliError. loop.json is written before the trace event, so a failed append leaves the loop closed without a loop.closed event.
